correctness.rationale: For every finite even population and every independent interior infection-risk vector, the disjoint pool assay count is m+2 sum of independent Bernoulli pool-positivity indicators. Variance reduction to 4 sum f(q_i q_j) is exact. Expanding all three four-point costs gives a crossing-never-strictly-best inequality. Lexicographic tie-breaking by least total span and greatest squared span proves a noncrossing global optimum without assuming strict probabilities. The parity-correct recurrence enumerates every noncrossing pairing, giving exact O(m^3) time/O(m^2) memory. Exact rational enumeration checks all 15 six-person matchings and supports, but does not replace, the universal algebraic proof.

value.rationale: Assay workload variability matters when second-stage retests must be resourced under fixed pair pooling. The exact arbitrary mixed-risk noncrossing structural theorem replaces unrestricted matchings with an inspectable interval recurrence for all population sizes, and the uniquely intermediate six-person optimum demonstrates a real gap beyond two extreme pairing recipes. It does not simply recompute a known table or assert routine reparameterization. Its application is conditional: if unrestricted individual tests are allowed, their count is deterministic and the variance-only objective becomes trivial.
